text:
jamie: Heads-up — saw a spike in the cost dashboard where 'cache savings' went negative for a small tenant group this morning. looks like routing fallbacks + prefetch accounting are double-counting somehow :confused:
anya: Oof. do you have a sample tenant id or route? could be sticky-routing falling back to a non-prefetchable variant and we still attribute the prefetch credit upstream
jamie: tenant: t-8421, route: /sdk/generate. I dumped a couple traces. noticed requests routed to model-v2 (no prefetch) after failure, but the dashboard shows a prefetch credit applied in the same epoch
mike: if the epochal accounting window aggregates by request_id incorrectly we can get negative net savings when fallback costs > credited savings. can you paste the event stream?
jamie: pasted a short dump to the thread:
```
EVENT stream for req=Rk3:
- route_decision: candidate=model-v1 (prefetch=true)
- prefetch_issued: tokens=32, cost_usd=0.0024
- route_fallback: to model-v2
- inference: model-v2 tokens=300, cost_usd=0.021
- cost_alloc: savings_applied=0.0024, direct_cost=0.021 -> net=+0.0186
- dashboard_epoch_rollup: shows savings=-0.004 (wha?)
```
anya: that dashboard_epoch_rollup line is the culprit — likely a sampling/merge bug where prefetch events get de-duped incorrectly across partition shards
sara: also check our sampling factor. we flat-sample invocations at 1% for the heavy tenants and then upsample in the rollup table. if prefetch events were included in raw but excluded in processed, rollups can misweight credits
mike: proposed quick sanity check: recompute the epoch rollup for that tenant from raw_event table with explicit join on request_id and sum. SQL:
```
SELECT request_id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN event_type='prefetch' THEN -cost_usd ELSE cost_usd END) as net_cost
FROM raw_events
WHERE tenant_id='t-8421' AND epoch_start >= '2026-03-18'
GROUP BY request_id;
```
jamie: ran that locally, and it lines up with the trace (net positive). so the raw_events look fine — the error must be in the rollup pipeline or the sampling correction multiplier
anya: two hypotheses: 1) rollup job merges incremental shards and applies correction factors from a separate table that was stale; 2) the routing telemetry proto changed field names (we renamed prefetch->prefetch_hint) and kafka consumer missed it so rollup treated prefetch events as unknown and applied negative default
sara: I can check the correction-factor table state. mike, can you grep the consumer logs for missing field warnings? @costbot do we have a historical diff for rollup vs raw for that tenant?
costbot: historical-diff job scheduled, will return a 2min summary (ETA ~90s) :gear:
mike: grep shows a handful of warnings around 02:11:14 where the consumer logged unknown_event_tag for prefetch_hint. looks like iso-2026 deploy changed the proto without bumping consumer code
anya: that matches #2. if the rollup consumer saw unknown prefetch events, what did the rollup code do? default to applying a zero or a negative placeholder?
mike: quick read of the rollup shard merge: if event_type not in expected set, it flags and sets cost_delta = -sample_correction * estimated_prefetch_credit (ack, legacy hack). so unknown event -> negative delta. sigh
jamie: great. so action plan: revert proto change deploy or bump consumer + backfill bad epochs. what do we want in the dashboard short-term?
sara: short-term: mark affected epoch in the UI as 'under investigation' and hide negative savings with a tooltip. long-term: patch consumer + run backfill for epochs 2026-03-18 00:00 -> 2026-03-18 06:00
anya: also add a telemetry enum compatibility test to CI for the consumer so deploys fail fast if proto enums diverge
mike: backfill plan: run recompute_rollup(tenant='t-8421', window='2026-03-18T00:00/06:00') in dry-run, validate sums match raw, then publish. I'll open the PR with consumer fix now
jamie: for the dashboard UX, can we show a breadcrumb of 'how savings were computed' on hover? e.g., breakdown: raw_cost, prefetch_credit, routing_fallback_penalty, sampling_correction. that would make these issues easier to triage
sara: yes, we already have those fields in the rollup, just not surfaced. small UI task — I'll own it.
anya: I'll add the CI proto-check, mike will patch consumer, sara will add UI breadcrumb + 'investigating' marker, and jamie will run backfill validation. timeline: today for hotfixes, backfill tomorrow AM
mike: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/p/infra/rollup-consumer/+/345 — fixes enum handling and adds unit test. cc @sara @anya
jamie: thanks. leaving traces here in case the billing team asks. :thumbsup:
anya: follow-up: we should also add an alert when per-tenant savings swing >50% relative to 1h baseline. this would've flagged it earlier. proposing alert name: econ.savings.delta.large
sara: agreed. I'll add the alert and a dashboard note.
mike: tagging release window: infra patch -> canary tonight. backfill gated on canary green.
jamie: done — adding this thread to the incident board for tracking.
